title: The realified kernel is $\iota$-real
statement:
Let $j:U_0\hookrightarrow\mathbf A^1_{k_0}$ be a dense open immersion with
$U_0=\mathbf A^1_{k_0}\setminus S_0$, and let $\mathcal M$ be an
irreducible lisse Weil
sheaf on $U_0$, unramified at infinity,
punctually $\iota$-pure of weight
$w$, with irreducible geometric fundamental representation of
[def-wf-fundamental-representation] and
middle extension that is
Fourier-nonexceptional. Put

$$
b:=\iota^{-1}(q^w),\qquad\text{so that}\qquad \iota(b)=q^w ,
\qquad
\mathcal M^\dagger:=\mathcal M^\vee\otimes\mathcal B_b ,
$$

the linear dual twisted by the constant
Weil twist, and let

$$
\mathcal K:=p_1^*(j_!\mathcal M)\otimes^L\mathcal K_\psi
\;\oplus\;
p_1^*\bigl(j_!(\mathcal M^\dagger)\bigr)\otimes^L\mathcal K_{\psi^{-1}}
$$

be the *realified kernel* on the Fourier square, the projections and
the Fourier kernel being those of
[def-fd-kernel] and the transform normalizations those of
[def-fd-transform]. Then $\mathcal K$ is
$\iota$-real in the sense of
[def-wf-iota-real]. More generally, the same conclusion holds, with
$b$, $\mathcal M^\dagger$ and $\mathcal K$ formed in the same way, for
*every* lisse Weil sheaf $\mathcal M$ on $U_0$ which is punctually
$\iota$-pure of weight $w$: the irreducibility, unramifiedness and
nonexceptionality hypotheses are not needed for the reality of the kernel.

proof.text:
Work with an arbitrary lisse $\mathcal M$ punctually pure of weight $w$; the more restrictive first assertion will follow. Since $q^w>0$, $b=\iota^{-1}(q^w)$ is nonzero. At a closed point $x\in U_0$ of degree $m$, let $A$ be Frobenius on $\mathcal M_{\bar x}$. By [lem-tw-dual-stalk-frobenius], the dual stalk operator is $(A^{-1})^*$. By the tensor and point-transport compatibility of [lem-tw-lisse-rational-realization] and the character $g\mapsto b^{\deg(g)}$ of [def-wf-constant-weil-twist], Frobenius on $\mathcal M^\dagger$ has matrix $b^m(A^{-1})^{\mathsf t}$. Its eigenvalues, with multiplicities, are $b^m/\alpha$ for the eigenvalues $\alpha$ of $A$: indeed transpose preserves determinant and $\det(tI-A^{-1})=\det(A)^{-1}\det(tA-I)$. Purity [def-weil-punctual-weights] gives $|\iota(\alpha)|^2=q^{mw}$. Thus
$$\iota(b^m/\alpha)=q^{mw}/\iota(\alpha)=\overline{\iota(\alpha)}.$$
The dual and tensor constructions here are lisse, and this computation uses no semisimplicity.

Write $W_0=\mathbf A^1_{k_0}\times\mathbf A^1_{k_0}$ and denote the evaluation function by $h(x,\xi)=x\xi$, to distinguish it from the scalar $b$. By [def-fd-kernel], $\mathcal K_\psi=h^*\mathcal L_\psi$. The sheaf $\mathcal L_\psi$ on the line is pure of weight zero by [lem-fd-as-purity] with $a=1$. For a closed $z\in W_0$, put $t=h(z)$ and $r=[\kappa(z):\kappa(t)]$. By [lem-fd-weil-pullback-local-frobenius], the eigenvalue $\lambda$ of the kernel at $z$ is the $r$-th power of the eigenvalue at $t$, so $|\iota(\lambda)|=1$. The rank-one assertion and inverse identity $\mathcal K_{\psi^{-1}}\cong\mathcal K_\psi^{-1}$ are exactly [prop-kernel-lisse]. In the lisse realization of [lem-tw-lisse-rational-realization], the tensor isomorphism $\mathcal K_\psi\otimes\mathcal K_{\psi^{-1}}\cong1$ intertwines Frobenius, so the eigenvalue of the inverse kernel is $\lambda^{-1}$. Put $L=\iota(\lambda)$; then $\overline L=L^{-1}$.

source.place: Step 1, the kernel eigenvalues are inverse complex conjugates

proof.text: Fix a closed $z\in W_0$. Apply [lem-fd-weil-pullback-local-frobenius] to $p_1:W_0\to\mathbf A^1_{k_0}$ and put $x=p_1(z)$, $e=[\kappa(z):\kappa(x)]$. Both zero extensions are constructible Weil sheaves by [lem-zl-immersion-weil-local-behavior](2); their stalks at $x$ are zero outside $U_0$, and on $U_0$ identify with the original stalks, compatibly with Frobenius. The pullback lemma applies to these sheaves even at the boundary. Tensoring with either lisse rank-one kernel is locally tensoring with the coefficient unit, so the displayed derived integrands are constructible sheaves in degree zero. At field coefficients $D^b_{ctf}=D^b_c$ by [def-weil-finite-tor-amplitude], so all these constructible inputs are in the domain of the point tensor comparison. For the geometric point $i_z:s=\operatorname{Spec}k\to W$ and either pulled-back zero extension $G$ and kernel $H$, first apply [lem-pur-derived-pullback-tensor-iso] to obtain $Li_z^*(G\otimes^L H)\cong Li_z^*G\otimes^L Li_z^*H$ in $D^b_c(s,\Qlb)$. Then [lem-sf-point-fibre-derived-tensor] identifies $\operatorname{Fib}_s$ of this tensor with $\operatorname{Fib}_s(Li_z^*G)\otimes^L_{\Qlb}\operatorname{Fib}_s(Li_z^*H)$. Thus if $x\notin U_0$ both fibres are $0\otimes^L\Qlb=0$ and the local factor of $\mathcal K$ is $1$. This includes all missing points, regardless of inertia of $\mathcal M$.

source.place: Steps 1–2, extension by zero and the boundary case

proof.text:
Now suppose $x\in U_0$. Let $E_x$ be the eigenvalue multiset on $\mathcal M_{\bar x}$ and put $a_\alpha=\iota(\alpha)$. By the pullback comparison [lem-fd-weil-pullback-local-frobenius] and the zero-extension identification from Step 3, the two pulled-back stalks have eigenvalues $\alpha^e$ and $(b^m/\alpha)^e$, respectively. Their complex images are $a_\alpha^e$ and $\overline{a_\alpha}^{\,e}$ by Step 1. On the open $p_1^{-1}(U_0)$ both factors are lisse. The tensor-and-fibre compatibility of [lem-tw-lisse-rational-realization] identifies their tensor Frobenius with tensor of the stalk operators. A rank-one factor with eigenvalue $\lambda$ scales the first operator by $\lambda$; the inverse kernel scales the second by $\lambda^{-1}$. Consequently the two complex eigenvalue multisets of the summands are
$$\{a_\alpha^eL:\alpha\in E_x\},\qquad\{\overline{a_\alpha}^{\,e}L^{-1}:\alpha\in E_x\}.$$
All powers and products preserve algebraic multiplicities, including when distinct eigenvalues acquire the same power.

source.place: Step 2, the two multisets on the Fourier square

proof.text:
For each occurrence of $\alpha\in E_x$, Step 2 gives
$$\overline{a_\alpha^eL}=\overline{a_\alpha}^{\,e}L^{-1}.$$
Thus conjugation exchanges the two multisets from Step 4. More explicitly, if $P(T)=\prod_{\alpha\in E_x}(1-a_\alpha^eLT)$, the local factor of the direct sum is $P(T)\overline{P(T)}$, where conjugation acts on coefficients; conjugating this product leaves it unchanged. Every coefficient is therefore real. At the boundary the factor is $1$ by Step 3. The local-factor definition [def-wf-iota-real] now says that $\mathcal K$ is $\iota$-real. Empty spectra give $P=1$; no assumption of distinct eigenvalues is used. The proof used only lissity and punctual purity of $\mathcal M$, proving both assertions.
